name: Spring SpEL expression injection
attack_scenario: Attacker submits T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('id') (or new ProcessBuilder(...)) as the expression string; parseExpression + getValue executes it on the server.
negative_test_hint: submit the expression "T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('id')" and assert it is rejected or treated as inert data, never parsed and evaluated as SpEL

exemplar.noncompliant:
Expression expr = parser.parseExpression(userSuppliedRule);
Object result = expr.getValue();
exemplar.explanation: SpringExpressionParser.parseExpression on attacker-controlled text evaluates arbitrary SpEL, e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...), giving remote code execution. Only literal expressions are safe; user data must be fed as evaluation-context variables, never parsed as the expression itself.
